arxiv-2501-02504.title: Watch Video, Catch Keyword: Context-aware Keyword Attention for Moment Retrieval and Highlight Detection
arxiv-2501-02504.creator: Sung Jin Um, Dongjin Kim, Sangmin Lee, Jung Uk Kim
arxiv-2501-02504.description: Abstract The goal of video moment retrieval and highlight detection is to identify specific segments and highlights based on a given text query. With the rapid growth of video content and the overlap between these tasks, recent works have addressed both simultaneously.

arxiv-2501-14565.title: Higher-Order Stochastic Dominance Constraints in Optimization
arxiv-2501-14565.creator: Rajmadan Lakshmanan, Alois Pichler, Miloš Kopa
arxiv-2501-14565.description: Abstract This contribution examines optimization problems that involve stochastic dominance constraints. These problems have uncountably many constraints. We develop methods to solve the optimization problem by reducing the constraints to a finite set of test points needed to verify stochastic dominance. This improves both theoretical understanding and computational efficiency.

Quinn, Karen A. Collins, Lyu Abe, Yuri Beletsky, Rafael Brahm, Knicole D. Colón, Zahra Essack, Tristan Guillot, Thomas Henning, Melissa J. Hobson, Keith Horne, Jon M.. arxiv-2508-06471.title: GLM-4.5: Agentic, Reasoning, and Coding (ARC) Foundation Models
arxiv-2508-06471.creator: GLM-4.5 Team
arxiv-2508-06471.description: Abstract We present GLM-4.5, an open-source Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model with 355B total parameters and 32B activated parameters, featuring a hybrid reasoning method that supports both thinking and direct response modes. Through multi-stage training on 23T tokens and comprehensive post-training with expert model iteration and reinforcement learning, GLM-4.

arxiv-2508-18403.title: Parity Breaking at Faceted Crystal Growth Fronts during Ice Templating
arxiv-2508-18403.creator: Kaihua Ji, Alain Karma
arxiv-2508-18403.description: Abstract Directional solidification of water-based solutions has emerged as a versatile technique to template hierarchical porous materials, but this nonequilibrium process remains incompletely understood. Here we use phase-field simulations to shed light on the mechanism that selects the growth direction of the lamellar ice structure that templates those materials.

arxiv-2510-23363.title: Interpretable Tile-Based Classification of Paclitaxel Exposure
arxiv-2510-23363.creator: Sean Fletcher, Gabby Scott, Douglas Currie, Xin Zhang, Yuqi Song, Bruce MacLeod
arxiv-2510-23363.description: Abstract Medical image analysis is central to drug discovery and preclinical evaluation, where scalable, objective readouts can accelerate decision-making. We address classification of paclitaxel (Taxol) exposure from phase-contrast microscopy of C6 glioma cells—a task with subtle dose differences that challenges full-image models.

arxiv-2512-05790.title: Learnability Window in Gated Recurrent Neural Networks
arxiv-2512-05790.creator: Lorenzo Livi
arxiv-2512-05790.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Livi. We develop a theoretical framework that explains how gating mechanisms determine the learnability window ℋ N \mathcal{H}_{N} of recurrent neural networks, defined as the largest temporal horizon over which gradient information remains statistically recoverable. While classical analyses emphasize numerical stability of Jacobian products, we show that stability alone is insufficient: learnability is governed instead by the effective learning rates μ t , ℓ \mu_{t,\ell} , per-lag and per-neuron quantities obtained from first-order expansions of gate-induced Jacobian products in Backpropagation Through Time.

pmc-10769519.title: Complete chloroplast genome of a traditional medicinal plant Luisia hancockii Rolfe 1896: genomic features and phylogenetic relationship within subtribe Aeridinae (Orchidaceae)
pmc-10769519.creator: Leqin Huang, Zhenyu Lu, Junfeng Wang, Huijuan Zhang, Ming Jiang
pmc-10769519.description: Luisia hancockii Rolfe 1896 is an epiphytic orchid species. In our present study, the whole chloroplast genome sequence of L. hancockii was de novo assembled by using high-throughput Illumina reads, and phylogenetic analysis was conducted within species of subtribe Aeridinae. The complete chloroplast genome sequence of L.

pmc-11402303.title: Venom exaptation and adaptation during the trophic switch to blood-feeding by kissing bugs
pmc-11402303.creator: Christina N. Zdenek, Fernanda C. Cardoso, Samuel D. Robinson, Raine S. Mercedes, Enriko R. Raidjõe, María José Hernandez-Vargas, Jiayi Jin, Gerardo Corzo, Irina Vetter, Glenn F. King, Bryan G. Fry, Andrew A. Walker
pmc-11402303.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryKissing bugs are known to produce anticoagulant venom that facilitates blood-feeding. However, it is unknown how this saliva evolved and if the venom produced by the entomophagous ancestors of kissing bugs would have helped or hindered the trophic shift. In this study, we show that venoms produced by extant predatory assassin bugs have strong anticoagulant properties mediated chiefly by proteolytic degradation of fibrinogen, and additionally contain anticoagulant disulfide-rich peptides.

pmc-11431402.title: Enhancement of Mechanical Properties of Zein-Based Nanofibers by Incorporation of Millet Gliadin
pmc-11431402.creator: Shumin Wang, Pengjie Wang, Siyuan Liu, Ran Wang, Yixuan Li, Xiaoyu Wang, Fazheng Ren, Jie Luo, Bing Fang, Ľubomír Lapčík
pmc-11431402.description: In this work, a novel reinforcing filler, millet gliadin (MG), was used for the improvement of the mechanical properties of zein nanofibers. The structural and physicochemical properties of MG were compared with those of zein, and the influence of MG on the morphology, physical properties, and molecular structure of zein nanofibers was investigated.

pmc-11467179.title: Trends in the incidence and survival of women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer from 1990 to 2019: a large population-based analysis
pmc-11467179.creator: Hongbo Huang, Tingting Wei, Aijie Zhang, Heng Zhang, Lingquan Kong, Yunhai Li, Fan Li
pmc-11467179.description: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer (BC) is the most prevalent subtype of BC and is generally correlated with a favorable prognosis. This study aimed to determine the incidence and survival trends among women diagnosed with hormone receptor-positive BC between 1990 and 2019.

pmc-11478845.title: Adaptation of the Food Literacy (FOODLIT) Tool for Turkish Adults: A Validity and Reliability Study
pmc-11478845.creator: Yasemin Ertaş Öztürk, Sevtap Kabalı, Yasemin Açar, Duygu Ağagündüz, Ferenc Budán, Ariana Saraiva, António Raposo
pmc-11478845.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Food literacy is associated with sustainable food systems and encourages individuals to adopt healthy eating habits. However, there is no validated method that can be used to measure food literacy related to sustainable food systems of Turkish adults. This research aimed to assess the validity and reliability of the Turkish adaptation of the “Food Literacy (FOODLIT) Tool” for Turkish adults. Methods: The study involved 328 people aged 19 to 58 years.

pmc-11509778.title: Surgical Management of Secondary Complex Microsurgical Reconstructions after Amputation and Severe Trauma Injuries: A Case Series
pmc-11509778.creator: Marcel Hoh, Sebastian Geis, Silvan Klein, Lukas Prantl, Vadym Burchak, Juergen H Dolderer, Jörg Eschweiler
pmc-11509778.description: Introduction: Secondary complex microsurgical reconstructions after amputation and severe trauma injuries are often necessary to optimize functional outcomes. Methods and Patients: We reviewed eight patients who underwent extensive reconstruction after severe trauma. The details of secondary procedures are further described in the article.

pmc-11512536.title: Scoping Review of Vicarious Post-Traumatic Growth Among Nurses: Current Knowledge and Research Gaps
pmc-11512536.creator: Yitong Cai, Ming Liu, Weixiang Luo, Jingping Zhang, Chaoran Qu
pmc-11512536.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundNurses frequently experience both direct and indirect trauma, leading to significant psychological challenges. While much research has focused on the negative impacts of such trauma, less attention has been given to vicarious post-traumatic growth (VPTG).

pmc-11585891.title: Advancements in surgical treatments for Huntington disease: From pallidotomy to experimental therapies
pmc-11585891.creator: Leo J.Y. Kim, Bornali Kundu, Paolo Moretti, Andres M. Lozano, Shervin Rahimpour
pmc-11585891.description: Huntington disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder characterized by choreic movements, behavioral changes, and cognitive impairment. The pathogenesis of this process is a consequence of mutant protein toxicity in striatal and cortical neurons. Thus far, neurosurgical management of HD has largely been limited to symptomatic relief of motor symptoms using ablative and stimulation techniques.

pmc-12363528.title: Developing the risk prediction model (ProlncSig) from lipoxygenase pathway-related lncRNAs for prognosis prediction in breast cancer
pmc-12363528.creator: Xiaoyu Fu, Weixing Wang, Bradley M Downs, Juanjuan Li
pmc-12363528.description: Alterations in cellular metabolism are known to play a crucial role in the development and progression of cancer. The lipoxygenase pathway, which controls unsaturated fatty acid metabolism, has been shown to regulate tumour progression and is commonly altered in breast cancer. In this study, we first obtained 11 lipoxygenase pathway genes from the Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB).

pmc-12748985.title: See through metallic sensor implemented using proximity resonant coupling
pmc-12748985.creator: Thamer Almoneef, Shehroze Amir, Muhammad Amin, Omar Siddiqui
pmc-12748985.description: Metal detection plays an important role in applications ranging from security to industrial quality control. This work presents a novel ground-less circular patch resonator which behaves as an open stub, engineered for high-sensitivity detection of metallic objects. The key innovation lies in utilizing electric field coupling between the stub’s top surface and nearby metallic targets.

pmc-13031813.title: Multifunctional hierarchical Ni2CoS4 structures for combating drug-resistant infections and colorectal cancer via piezocatalytic ROS generation
pmc-13031813.creator: Karzan Qurbani, Omid Amiri, Haider Hamzah
pmc-13031813.description: The global rise of multidrug-resistant infections and cancer underscores the need for multifunctional therapeutic platforms. This study presents the synthesis, optimization, and biomedical assessment of sonicated hierarchical Ni₂CoS₄ structures, with sample N3 identified as optimal among seven hydrothermally synthesized formulations. N3 exhibited uniform morphology, high crystallinity, and redox-active architecture, as confirmed by XRD, SEM, TEM, and BET (8.19 m²/g).

pmc-13038487.title: Safer conception needs of women living with HIV in Southern Ghana: a qualitative study
pmc-13038487.creator: Ellen E Klutsey, Regis Rugira Marie Modeste, Deliwe R Phetlhu
pmc-13038487.description: Background:Antiretroviral therapy (ART) has improved the quality of life of women living with HIV (WLHIV), increasing their intention and attempts at having children. Educating WLHIV on safer conception strategies helps them to navigate the periconception HIV transmission risk. However, understanding the context-specific needs of WLHIV is crucial in tailoring the provision of SC services.

pmc-13097853.title: Determinants and outcomes of adverse drug reactions among people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy in Nigeria
pmc-13097853.creator: Victoria P. Etuk, Ikeola A. Adeoye, Mobolaji M. Salawu, Olufunmilayo I. Fawole
pmc-13097853.description: Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) to Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) among people living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA) can significantly affect treatment adherence, viral suppression and contribute to HIV-related morbidity and mortality. ADRs to long-term ART use is not well understood in resource-constrained countries like Nigeria. This study identified the determinants and outcomes of ADRs to ART among PLWHA in Nigeria.

pmc-13118352.title: Catalase Specifically Binds Antipsychotic Clozapine: Experimental and In Silico Insights into Interactions, Complex Stability, and Dose-Dependent Enzyme Activity Modulation
pmc-13118352.creator: Tamara Vasović, Milica Radibratović, Dušan Spasić, Simeon Minić, Čedo Miljević, Nikola Gligorijević, Milan Nikolić
pmc-13118352.description: Oxidative stress is intrinsically linked to mental disorders, involving an imbalance between reactive species and antioxidant defenses, where catalase is an essential, ubiquitous antioxidant enzyme. The pleiotropic effects of antipsychotic drugs, used for schizophrenia and mood disorders, are not fully elucidated at the molecular level.

pmc-13410517.title: Interfacial Regulation by a NiO x Overlayer Enables Enhanced Near‐Infrared Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting
pmc-13410517.creator: Xiao‐Feng Shen, Kyle J Stephens, Dengyao Yang, Nick A Shepelin, Kuan‐Ting Wu, Kazuto Hatakeyama, Daniele Pergolesi, Shintaro Ida, Motonori Watanabe, Thomas Lippert

pmc-13578996.title: Neuromotor modules revealed by direct electrical stimulation of the human primary motor cortex
pmc-13578996.creator: Jodie J. Xie, Subing Huang, Kelvin Y. S. Lau, Amy H. S. Kong, Rosa H. M. Chan, Peter Y. M. Woo, Vincent C. K. Cheung
pmc-13578996.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SignificanceThis study has advanced our understanding of the origin of muscle synergies in humans by utilizing direct electrophysiological evidence obtained from cortical stimulation in patients undergoing glioma resection. Beyond demonstrating the neural origin of muscle synergies in humans by exploiting a neurosurgical procedure, this study also provides a detailed topographical description of how human muscle synergies may be represented over the M1 while at the same time revealing two M1 subdivisions with distinct synergy organizations.

pmc-13663311.title: Papillary fibroelastoma of the mitral valve initially suspected as myxoma: a case report of resection via minimally invasive approach
pmc-13663311.creator: Shota Inoue, Hayate Nomura, Yukihiro Hayatsu
pmc-13663311.description: BackgroundPapillary fibroelastomas typically arise from the cardiac valves, whereas cardiac myxomas rarely originate from the valves. Distinguishing these tumors intraoperatively can be challenging.Case presentationAn 81-year-old man was referred for evaluation of an incidental cardiac mass. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a mobile 10-mm mass attached to the P1 segment of the posterior mitral leaflet.
